items.answer: Immersion in virtual reality (VR) means that the user's senses are blocked so that the user receives no input from the real-world environment and receives input only from the virtual world.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.
Presence is the psychological side that captures whether a user perceives the immersive qualities that are generated.

Cybersickness (CS), also known in the literature as visually induced motion sickness (VIMS), is a condition that can affect individuals when they interact with virtual reality (VR) technology and is primarily relevant to virtual reality.

The formative years of virtual reality are the second phase of its historical evolution, roughly 1950 to 1990 after computers appeared in the 1940s, beginning with development of head-mounted displays (HMDs) in the 1950s and ending with popularization of the term virtual reality in the late 1980s.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the six VR-content factors that affect cybersickness?
options: Field of view
Audio loudness
Headset type
User's age
questions.explanation: The six VR-content factors are visual motion, means of locomotion, field of view, type of content, duration, and visual complexity.

questions.question: How does visual motion relate to cybersickness?
options: Higher visual motion is irrelevant to risk, and the way content moves determines severity.
Higher visual motion can increase risk, but the way content moves does not affect severity.
Higher visual motion can increase risk, and the way content moves affects severity.
Lower visual motion can increase risk, and the way content moves affects severity.
questions.explanation: Visual motion is a primary cause of cybersickness: higher visual motion can increase risk, and the way the content moves also affects cybersickness and its severity.

questions.question: What is vection?
options: The sensation of self-motion
The preference for adventurous virtual content
The rate at which visual motion changes
The sensation of the virtual environment rotating
questions.explanation: Vection is the sensation of self-motion, is highest when motion is sensed in peripheral stimuli, and is positively correlated with visual motion stimulus.

questions.question: What does brief exposure to turbulent visual motion do to cybersickness?
options: Alone it is not enough to induce it, but longer exposure can induce it.
Alone it is enough to induce it immediately.
Alone it matters only when combined with faster speed.
Alone it prevents it, and longer exposure reduces it.
questions.explanation: Brief exposure to turbulent visual motion alone is not enough to induce cybersickness, but longer exposure to turbulent visual motion can induce it.

questions.question: How does rotation affect cybersickness?
options: It increases with angular velocity and is more intense around the z axis than the x and y axes.
It increases with angular velocity and is more intense around the x and y axes than the z axis.
It is unaffected by angular velocity and is more intense around the z axis than the x and y axes.
It decreases with angular velocity and is more intense around the x and y axes than the z axis.
questions.explanation: Cybersickness increases with increasing angular velocity and is more intense when rotation takes place around the x and y axes than around the z axis.

data.text: The design of virtual environments can have a significant impact on the likelihood and severity of cybersickness. Six content factors affect cybersickness, with visual motion being a primary cause influenced by the amount and manner of movement. Vection, the sensation of self-motion, is highest in peripheral stimuli and correlates with visual motion. Additionally, factors such as height, speed, duration of exposure, viewpoint, and angular velocity also influence cybersickness.
points: The design of virtual environments can have a significant impact on the likelihood and severity of cybersickness.
Six content factors affect cybersickness: visual motion, means of locomotion, field of view, type of content, duration, and visual complexity.
Visual motion is a primary cause of cybersickness, and higher visual motion can increase the risk while the manner of movement affects its severity.
Vection, the sensation of self-motion, is highest in peripheral stimuli and correlates with visual motion.
Cybersickness is also influenced by height, speed, duration of exposure, viewpoint, and angular velocity.

questions.question: Why is means of locomotion considered a content-related factor in cybersickness?
options: It increases the angular velocity of the user's head.
It makes virtual objects rotate around the x and y axes.
It can create a sensory mismatch between virtual and physical movement.
It increases the field of view captured by the display.
questions.explanation: Means of locomotion describes how a user moves in a virtual world, and a sensory mismatch between virtual and physical movements can cause discomfort and disorientation that lead to cybersickness.

questions.question: Which statement best describes how control over motion affects cybersickness in virtual reality?
options: More control increases presence, and greater presence generally reduces cybersickness.
More control decreases presence, and lower presence generally increases cybersickness.
Less control increases presence, and greater presence generally reduces cybersickness.
More control affects cybersickness directly through visual motion rather than presence.
questions.explanation: Control over motion directly affects presence, with more control producing greater presence, and greater presence in virtual reality generally reduces cybersickness.

questions.question: Which statement about virtual reality control mechanisms and cybersickness is supported by research studies?
options: Hand-based motion control leads to significantly more cybersickness than whole-body motion control.
Hand-based and whole-body motion control lead to the same amount of cybersickness.
Hand-based motion control leads to significantly less cybersickness than whole-body motion control.
Whole-body motion control leads to significantly less cybersickness than hand-based motion control.
questions.explanation: Research studies find that hand-based motion control leads to significantly less cybersickness than whole-body motion control.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares teleportation and naturalistic free movement for cybersickness?
options: Teleportation, an instantaneous transition, reduces cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement.
Teleportation, a gradual transition, reduces cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement.
Naturalistic free movement, such as walking, running, and jumping, reduces cybersickness compared with teleportation.
Teleportation, an instantaneous transition, increases cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement.
questions.explanation: Teleportation is an instantaneous transition, and it is found to reduce cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement such as walking, running, and jumping.

data.text: Locomotion is a content-related factor because sensory mismatches between virtual and physical movements can cause cybersickness. Control over motion affects presence, where more control leads to greater presence and generally reduces cybersickness. Hand-based motion control and instantaneous transitions like teleportation are found to reduce cybersickness compared to whole-body motion and naturalistic free movement such as walking, running, and jumping.
points: Locomotion is a content-related factor where sensory mismatches can cause cybersickness.
Control over motion affects presence, and more control generally leads to less cybersickness.
Hand-based motion control leads to significantly less cybersickness than whole-body motion control.
Teleportation is found to reduce cybersickness compared to naturalistic free movement.

questions.question: In virtual reality, what does field of view describe?
options: The method by which a user moves through a virtual world
The amount of time a user spends in a virtual environment
The movement experienced by a user in a virtual environment
The extent to which a headset display captures the user's field of vision
questions.explanation: Field of view is the extent to which the VR display captures the user's field of vision.

questions.question: What is a general effect of a larger field of view in virtual reality?
options: It captures less of the visual field and can increase immersion
It captures more of the visual field and can decrease immersion
It captures more of the visual field and can increase immersion
It captures less of the visual field and can decrease immersion
questions.explanation: A larger field of view captures a larger field of vision and generally results in greater immersion.

questions.question: What can happen if a virtual reality field of view is made excessively narrow?
options: It can decrease immersion and increase head movement, increasing cybersickness
It can reduce fast movements and abrupt alterations, decreasing cybersickness
It can replace stormy weather with clear weather, decreasing cybersickness
It can increase immersion and decrease head movement, decreasing cybersickness
questions.explanation: An excessively narrow field of view can decrease immersion and increase head movement, which may exacerbate or increase cybersickness.

questions.question: Which type of virtual reality content is more likely to induce cybersickness?
options: Content shown in clear weather conditions
Neutral and static content
Pleasant general content
Action content with fast movements and abrupt alterations
questions.explanation: Action content, fast movements, and abrupt alterations are found to induce more cybersickness than neutral and static content.

questions.question: How does virtual terrain influence cybersickness during travel?
options: Regular bumps or irregular terrain are more likely to cause cybersickness than flat terrain
Flat terrain is more likely to cause cybersickness than regular bumps or irregular terrain
Flat terrain and bumpy terrain have the same likelihood of causing cybersickness
Regular bumps or irregular terrain are less likely to cause cybersickness than flat terrain
questions.explanation: Travel over regular bumps and irregular terrain is more likely to cause cybersickness than the same travel over flat terrain.

data.text: Field of view (FOV) determines how much of the user's vision is captured and impacts susceptibility to cybersickness. While a larger FOV increases immersion, reducing it can alleviate symptoms, although an excessively narrow FOV may increase head movement and exacerbate cybersickness. Furthermore, action content, horror genres, bumpy terrain, and stormy weather are more likely to induce cybersickness, though users accustomed to adrenaline sports may experience less severity from action content.
points: Field of view (FOV) determines how much of the user's vision is captured and affects susceptibility to cybersickness.
While a larger FOV increases immersion, reducing it can help alleviate cybersickness.
An excessively narrow FOV can decrease immersion and increase head movement, which may exacerbate cybersickness.
Action content, horror genres, bumpy terrain, and stormy weather are more likely to induce cybersickness.
Users accustomed to adrenaline sports may experience less cybersickness from action content.

questions.question: Which condition is associated with greater cybersickness when using virtual reality?
options: Reducing the field of view
Prolonged exposure through a head-mounted display
Brief exposure through a head-mounted display
Viewing neutral static content
questions.explanation: VR exposure duration is an important factor in cybersickness, and prolonged exposure through HMDs leads to greater cybersickness.

questions.question: In VR navigation tasks, what does longer exposure time do to the effect of the locomotion controller on cybersickness?
options: It can make that effect identical for all controllers
It can make that effect depend only on weather
It can make that effect more complicated
It can remove that effect
questions.explanation: Cybersickness increases with VR exposure time during navigation, and longer duration further complicates the effect of the locomotion technique.

questions.question: What happens to cybersickness during continuous exposure to live-action 180-degree videos?
options: It increases as exposure time grows
It is greatest for very brief exposures
It remains constant as exposure time grows
It declines as exposure time grows
questions.explanation: Continuous exposure to live-action 180-degree videos results in higher cybersickness, and the increase grows with exposure time.

questions.question: Which type of visual environment is more likely to induce cybersickness?
options: A flat-terrain scene without bumpy movement
A clear-weather scene with calm conditions
A scene with few static objects of similar size
A scene with many objects of different shapes, sizes, and movements
questions.explanation: Visual complexity is positively correlated with cybersickness symptoms, so scenes with more varied objects, sizes, and movements are more likely to induce it.

data.text: Prolonged exposure through HMDs and continuous exposure to live-action 180-degree videos lead to greater cybersickness. CS also increases with exposure time when using different locomotion controllers, with the effect further complicated by longer duration. Additionally, visual complexity is positively correlated with cybersickness.
points: Prolonged exposure through HMDs leads to greater cybersickness.
CS increases with exposure time when using different locomotion controllers, with the effect further complicated by longer duration.
Continuous exposure to live-action 180-degree videos results in higher cybersickness.
Visual complexity is positively correlated with cybersickness.

questions.question: In the input-process-output framework for cybersickness measurement, what are the three components?
options: The questionnaire, the sickness score, and the intervention
The measurement input, the measurement technique, and the measurement output
The user, the virtual world, and the headset
The input, the output, and the virtual environment
questions.explanation: The framework relies on the input provided for measurement, the measurement technique itself, and the output generated.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used as an input for measuring cybersickness?
options: A sickness score
A real-time evaluation
A manual technique
Questionnaire-based information
questions.explanation: Cybersickness inputs can be questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric information, behavioral information, or content-based information.

questions.question: Which of the following describes how cybersickness measurement can be performed?
options: As real-time evaluation while the experience is taking place
As a numerical sickness score
As a questionnaire rating scale
As a binary discomfort class
questions.explanation: The measurement technique can be manual, automated, machine learning-based, or real-time evaluation during the experience.

questions.question: Questionnaire-based cybersickness scales are most commonly administered...
options: Before or after the experience
Only before the experience
Only while the experience is taking place
Only after the experience
questions.explanation: Before and after administration is the most common timing, while administration during the experience is occasional.

questions.question: A widely used cybersickness questionnaire that contains oculomotor, disorientation, and nausea subscales was best described as...
options: Designed primarily to assess overall discomfort in virtual environments
Created mainly to measure susceptibility to cybersickness
Adapted for virtual reality although it was not originally designed for it
Originally designed specifically for virtual reality head-mounted displays
questions.explanation: The Simulator Sickness Questionnaire contains those subscales, but it was not originally designed for virtual reality and was adapted for that context.

data.text: Measurement techniques for cybersickness (CS) rely on three components: the input provided for measurement, the measurement technique itself, and the output generated. Inputs for measuring CS can be questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric information, behavioral information, and content-based information. The measurement technique can be manual, automated, machine learning-based, or real-time evaluation, while the output can be binary classes, multiple classes, or a numerical sickness score. Questionnaire-based inputs are a common method that uses self-report questionnaires or scales to rate users' discomfort or disorientation on a numerical scale.
points: Measurement techniques for cybersickness (CS) rely on three components: the input provided for measurement, the measurement technique itself, and the output generated.
Inputs for measuring CS can be questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric information, behavioral information, and content-based information.
The measurement technique for CS can be manual, automated, machine learning-based, or real-time evaluation.
The output of CS measurement can be binary classes, multiple classes, or a sickness score that is a number.
Questionnaire-based inputs are common methods that use self-report questionnaires or scales to rate users' discomfort or disorientation on a numerical scale.

questions.question: Why are physiological or biometric inputs used to detect cybersickness?
options: Because questionnaire-based input is objective and always reliable
Because physiological inputs directly measure hardware latency and virtual reality content
Because biometric inputs can only produce a binary sickness class
Because questionnaire-based input can be subjective, inaccurate, and unreliable
questions.explanation: Questionnaire-based inputs can be subjective, are prone to inaccuracies, and may not always be reliable, so physiological or biometric inputs are used.

questions.question: Which input is specifically described as widely used for detecting cybersickness?
options: Behavioral information
Content-based information
Electroencephalogram (EEG)
Questionnaire-based ratings
questions.explanation: EEG is identified as one of the widely used physiological or biometric inputs for detecting cybersickness.

questions.question: Which of the following sets contains only physiological or biometric inputs for detecting cybersickness?
options: Hardware, virtual reality content, and user age
Heart rate, electrocardiogram, and respiration signals
Questionnaire ratings, behavioral information, and content-based information
Binary classes, multiple classes, and sickness scores
questions.explanation: Heart rate, electrocardiogram, and respiration signals are listed as physiological or biometric inputs, while the other sets are not all from that list.

data.text: Physiological or biometric inputs can be used to detect cybersickness because questionnaire-based inputs can be subjective and unreliable. Electroencephalogram (EEG) is one of the widely used inputs for detecting cybersickness. Other signals such as heart rate and galvanic skin response can also be used for detection.
points: Physiological or biometric inputs can be used to detect cybersickness because questionnaire-based inputs can be subjective and unreliable.
Electroencephalogram (EEG) is one of the widely used physiological or biometric inputs for detecting cybersickness.
Many other physiological or biometric inputs, such as heart rate and galvanic skin response, can also be used for detection.

questions.question: Which of the following is a behavioral input for measuring cybersickness?
options: Galvanic skin response
Postural sway
Heart rate
Electroencephalogram (EEG)
questions.explanation: Behavioral inputs for measuring cybersickness include blink rate, head and body movement, the manner of those movements, and postural sway.

questions.question: How can postural sway be monitored during virtual reality exposure for measuring cybersickness?
options: By using axial movements or changes in the user's center of pressure
By measuring the user's heart rate
By asking users to complete a sickness questionnaire
By detecting optical flow in the virtual world
questions.explanation: Postural sway can be monitored during VR exposure using axial movements or changes in the user's center of pressure.

questions.question: Why can postural sway be used to indicate cybersickness severity?
options: Because postural instability is positively correlated with cybersickness severity
Because postural sway is a subjective questionnaire-based input
Because postural sway is a content-based input
Because postural instability is negatively correlated with cybersickness severity
questions.explanation: Postural instability is positively correlated with the severity of cybersickness, so postural sway can indicate that severity.

questions.question: Which of the following is a content-based input for measuring cybersickness?
options: Heart rate
Blink rate
Optical flow
Postural sway
questions.explanation: Content-based inputs for measuring cybersickness include optical flow, depth cues, and exceptional motion velocity.

questions.question: Which option correctly names the four input categories for measuring cybersickness?
options: Questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric, behavioral, and content-based inputs
Questionnaire-based, behavioral, visual, and auditory inputs
Questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric, auditory, and behavioral inputs
Physiological and biometric, behavioral, content-based, and hardware-based inputs
questions.explanation: The four input categories are questionnaire-based inputs, physiological and biometric inputs, behavioral inputs, and content-based inputs.

data.text: Behavioral inputs for measuring cybersickness include various movements and postural sway, where postural instability correlates positively with severity. Content-based inputs consist of optical flow, depth cues, and motion velocity. These inputs fall into four categories: questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric, behavioral, and content-based.
points: Behavioral inputs for measuring cybersickness include blink rate, head and body movements, and postural sway.
Postural instability correlates positively with the severity of cybersickness.
Content-based inputs for measuring cybersickness include optical flow, depth cues, and exceptional motion velocity.
Cybersickness can be measured using four categories of inputs: questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric, behavioral, and content-based.

questions.question: Cybersickness measurement techniques based on input are broadly divided into which two types?
options: Physiological measurement and behavioral measurement
Manual evaluation and machine learning-based automated evaluation
Real-time evaluation and offline evaluation
Questionnaire-based assessment and content-based assessment
questions.explanation: Input-based cybersickness measurement techniques are broadly manual, based on human intervention, or machine learning/automated, using automated algorithms.

questions.question: What is the typical procedure for manual cybersickness evaluation?
options: An algorithm automatically classifies physiological or biometric signals.
Postural sway is tracked during exposure to compute a sickness score.
A person distributes a questionnaire, collects feedback, and reviews responses to judge severity, onset, or possibility.
Content-based features such as optical flow are compared with thresholds.
questions.explanation: Manual evaluation is entirely based on human intervention and typically uses questionnaire-based assessment, where a person collects and reviews responses to decide severity, onset, or possibility.

questions.question: Which inputs can be used to train models for machine learning-based cybersickness evaluation?
options: Psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs
Only content-based visual features
Only postural sway measurements
Only questionnaire-based responses
questions.explanation: Machine learning-based evaluation can use psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs to train models that automatically determine cybersickness.

questions.question: What is a defining property of transparent models used in machine learning-based cybersickness evaluation?
options: They conceal the decision-making process while producing an automatic score.
They provide clear insight into the decision-making process and easily understood inner workings.
They rely solely on user-completed questionnaires after VR exposure.
They require no input features and infer cybersickness from hardware settings.
questions.explanation: Transparent models provide clear insight into the decision-making process and their inner workings can easily be understood.

data.text: Cybersickness measurement techniques are broadly manual evaluation based on human intervention and machine learning-based evaluation using automated algorithms. Manual evaluation typically uses questionnaire-based assessment, while machine learning-based evaluation can use psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs to train models. These models can be transparent, such as stepwise regression analysis, which provide clear insight into the decision-making process.
points: Cybersickness measurement techniques are broadly manual evaluation and machine learning-based evaluation.
Manual evaluation is based on human intervention and typically uses questionnaire-based assessment to decide the severity, onset, or possibility of cybersickness.
Machine learning-based evaluation can use psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs to train models that automatically determine cybersickness.
Machine learning-based evaluation can use transparent models that provide clear insight into the decision-making process.
Stepwise regression analysis can be considered a transparent model used to measure cybersickness using physiological signals.

questions.question: Why can giving a user more control over movement in a virtual world reduce their risk of cybersickness?
questions.reference_answer: Control over motion in a virtual world directly affects presence, the psychological side that captures whether a user perceives the immersive qualities that are generated. Greater presence in virtual reality generally reduces cybersickness, while more control means greater presence and less control means lower presence. Therefore, giving users more movement control can lower cybersickness through increased presence.

questions.question: Why is changing the field of view of a virtual reality headset a trade-off between immersion and cybersickness?
questions.reference_answer: A field of view is the extent to which the display captures the user's field of vision, and a larger field of view generally results in greater immersion. Reducing the field of view can be an effective way to alleviate symptoms of cybersickness. However, an excessively narrow field of view can decrease immersion and increase head movement to look for things in the environment, which may exacerbate or increase cybersickness.

questions.question: Why can longer exposure to turbulent visual motion induce cybersickness while brief exposure alone may not?
questions.reference_answer: Visual motion is one of the primary causes of cybersickness, and higher visual motion can increase the risk, while the way the content moves also affects severity. Vection, the sensation of self-motion, is highest when motion is sensed in peripheral stimuli and is positively correlated with visual motion stimulus. Brief exposure to turbulent visual motion alone is not enough to induce cybersickness, but longer exposure to turbulent visual motion can induce cybersickness.

questions.question: Why can physiological or biometric signals complement questionnaire-based reports when measuring cybersickness?
questions.reference_answer: Questionnaire-based input uses self-report ratings and is a subjective category of input for measuring cybersickness. Physiological or biometric inputs are objective, and they can detect cybersickness because questionnaires can be subjective, prone to inaccuracies, and may not always be reliable. Using them together can combine user-reported discomfort with objective signals.
